PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal diagnosis requested following high-risk non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) result for trisomy 13.

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome. Peak area ratios were calculated for all heterozygous markers. Normal diallelic ratios range from 0.8-1.4. Triallelic patterns or skewed ratios (>1.8 or <0.65) indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal female pattern
- D13S631: 1.02
- D13S258: 1.11
- D13S742: 0.98
- D13S628: 1.05

Chromosome 18: Normal female pattern
- D18S391: 0.95
- D18S390: 1.08
- D18S535: 1.01
- D18S386: 0.99

Chromosome 21: Normal female pattern
- D21S1435: 1.12
- D21S1411: 0.94
- D21S1412: 1.03
- D21S1437: 0.97

Sex Chromosomes: XX (Female)
- AMELX/Y: X only
- DXYS218: Single peak
- X22: Two peaks, ratio 1.06

CONCLUSION
Normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18 and 21. No abnormality detected in uncultured amniotic fluid sample.

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR result shows no evidence of trisomy 13, 18 or 21 in the fetal sample. The normal result supersedes the positive NIPT screening for trisomy 13, indicating no chromosomal abnormality for these chromosomes. NIPT is a screening test with known false positive rates, particularly for trisomy 13 which has a positive predictive value of approximately 45-50%.

LIMITATIONS
QF-PCR detects whole chromosome aneuploidies for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y only. This test will not detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Mosaicism below 20-30%
- Segmental chromosomal imbalances
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is needed for this sample based on the current clinical indication. The pregnancy can be managed as chromosomally normal for the tested chromosomes.

If there are ongoing clinical concerns or ultrasound abnormalities, please contact the laboratory to discuss additional testing options including chromosomal microarray or karyotype analysis.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FRCPath
Consultant Clinical Scientist
